content: 1. Rifabutin reduces the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of elvitegravir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapy. 2. Rifampin significantly decreases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Coadministration of elvitegravir with CYP3A inducers, such as rifampin or rifapentine, may lead to reduced plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and/or protease inhibitors, resulting in loss of therapeutic efficacy and potential resistance. Avoid coadministration. 4. Rifapentine decreases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. St. John’s Wort reduces the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapy. 6. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of riociguat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapy. 8. Ritonavir increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration due to the risk of increased rivaroxaban exposure and bleeding. 10. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapy. 11. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of ruxolitinib topical by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is not recommended due to the risk of cardiovascular effects, including QT prolongation, palpitations, and sinus tachycardia. 13. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapy. 14. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per its monograph. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for three elimination half-lives. 15. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors combined with moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 16. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapy. 17. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 18. Sotorasib reduces the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) by inducing P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or refer to the prescribing information for dosage adjustments. 19. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration upon resumption. 20. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapy. 21. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust tadalafil dosage for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) or erectile dysfunction (ED) as per specific recommendations. 23. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of talazoparib by inhibiting breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP). Monitor for adverse reactions if coadministration cannot be avoided. 24. Cobicistat decreases the therapeutic effect of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing its conversion to the active metabolite. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapy. 25. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 27. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of teniposide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapy. 28. Tepotinib increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporter activity. Reduce the TAF dosage if coadministration is unavoidable. 29. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of ticagrelor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction is required, and adjustments should be made if the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued. 31. Acalabrutinib increases the plasma concentration of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 32. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 33. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the plasma concentration of elvitegravir by forming ionic complexes in the gastrointestinal tract. Separate doses by at least 2 hours. 34. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended during coadministration. 35. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of amitriptyline by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect. 36. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of amoxapine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect. 38. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of apalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Apalutamide decreases the plasma concentration of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) by inducing its elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of apixaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 41. Berotralstat increases the plasma concentration of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporter activity. Monitor or titrate the TAF dose as needed. 42. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the aripiprazole dose by 25% or 50% depending on the coadministered inhibitors. 43. Cobicistat decreases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced antimalarial efficacy or QT prolongation. 44. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the plasma concentration of elvitegravir by forming ionic complexes in the gastrointestinal tract. Separate doses by at least 2 hours. 45. Atazanavir increases the plasma concentration of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust elvitegravir dosage as per specific recommendations. 46. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust atogepant dosage to 10 mg daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 47. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 20 mg/day of atorvastatin. 48. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of avatrombopag by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust avatrombopag starting dose when treating ITP with dual CYP2C9/3A4 inhibitors. 49. Belzutifan decreases the plasma concentration of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 50. Belzutifan decreases the plasma concentration of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider increasing the dose of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates if coadministration is unavoidable. 51. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for potentially fatal respiratory depression. 52. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of berotralstat by inhibiting BCRP. Monitor for adverse effects when coadministered with a BCRP inhibitor. 53. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration of betrixaban by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporter activity. Reduce betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, then 40 mg daily. 54. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Bosentan decreases the plasma concentration of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust bosentan dosage as per prescribing information. 56. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 58. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if coadministered with moderate CYP2D6 and strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 59. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
